$comment: Two forms of one prayer, named for the traditions that sing them. The bundle shipped the Byzantine form from the start without saying so — acclamation thrice, Glory Be, the short acclamation, acclamation — and it stays the default, byte-identical (the engine tests pin its six steps). The Syriac form is how Erez prays it (2026-08-07): the acclamation thrice, then the Kyrie. The Kyrie is ONE composed step, not three — the Vicariate's Hebrew (sent 2026-08-08, unvocalized as it arrived) is the full threefold form in a single line, ישוע שמענו, המשיח עזרנו, האדון חננו ≙ Kyrie eleison, Christe eleison, Kyrie eleison, and a composed line cannot be a repeated step without praying nine invocations. Every language carries the threefold form; Erez's rite overlays it with his own ה׳ רחם־נא said thrice. Only the Hebrew heading still waits on the prayer book (allowlisted, falls back to the bundle's Latin).
